string.name: check_db_help
string.value:
Checks the integrity of the local card collection and repairs abnormal data.

Issues that may be fixed:
• Invalid card properties or cards missing a note
• Wrong field count, missing or duplicate templates
• Missing decks, invalid review log properties
• Invalid UTF-8 characters, future timestamps
• Corrupt collection file (restore from backup)

When to use:
• You suspect abnormal card data (e.g. cards disappeared, review logs messed up)
• After a sync conflict or a forced app shutdown
• Step 4 of Anki's official troubleshooting flow (Tools → Check Database)

Note: The check rebuilds and optimizes the database; it normally does not lose data. If it reports the collection is corrupt, please restore from an automatic backup.

string.name: settings_fsrs_help
string.value:
FSRS schedules reviews from memory state, ratings and desired retention. This switch affects the entire collection; turning it off uses SM-2.

This app enables FSRS on first initialization. Enabling it here recalculates affected schedules, which may take time for a large collection. A later decision to turn it off is retained.

Enter learning and relearning steps as positive numbers of minutes separated by spaces, such as 1 10. Unit suffixes such as 1d or 10m are not supported. Prefer manual FSRS steps that fit within one study day, or leave them empty for automatic short-term scheduling.

This app has no Optimize or Evaluate entry. Use an Anki client that supports those features and sync afterward if you need to fit parameters.

string.name: deck_learn_steps_help
string.value:
Delays during new-card learning, entered as positive numbers of minutes separated by spaces. For example, 1 10 means 1 minute then 10 minutes; enter 0.5 for 30 seconds or 120 for 2 hours. This field does not accept s, m, h or d suffixes.

Again returns to the first step; Good advances; Hard usually averages the first two delays on the first step and repeats the current step later. Easy can skip remaining steps.
SM-2 uses the graduating interval after learning. FSRS calculates subsequent intervals from its memory model and can schedule short-term learning when steps are empty. For manual FSRS steps, prefer short delays you can complete within one study day.

string.name: deck_relearn_steps_help
string.value:
Relearning delays after rating a review card Again. Enter positive numbers of minutes separated by spaces, without unit suffixes; for example, 10 means 10 minutes.

With SM-2, empty steps skip fixed relearning steps; the next interval depends on the lapse multiplier, minimum lapse interval and other limits, rather than always being 1 day. FSRS computes intervals from memory state and may still schedule short-term relearning when steps are empty.

string.name: deck_newPerDay_help
string.value:
The maximum number of new cards introduced each day. If you study fewer than the limit or miss a day, it does not accumulate — the next day starts again at the original limit.
Official advice: new cards sharply increase your near-term review load, so keep this at least 10x smaller than the daily review limit. Official rule of thumb — consistently learning 20 new cards a day stabilizes your daily reviews at about 200.
Example: set to 20 and you learn at most 20 new cards today; the rest roll over to tomorrow.
Note: the review limit also caps new cards — with a review limit of 200 and 190 reviews already waiting, at most 10 new cards appear today; once the review quota is exhausted, new cards stop appearing by default (enable “New cards ignore review limit” in advanced settings to change this).

string.name: deck_reviewsPerDay_help
string.value:
The maximum number of due review cards shown each day; once reached, no more reviews appear even if more are waiting. Interday learning cards count toward this limit before review cards.
Example: set to 200 and even if 300 cards are due, only 200 are shown today; the rest roll over to tomorrow.
This limit also constrains new cards: once the review quota is exhausted, new cards stop appearing by default.
Official tip: the limit is great for smoothing occasional due-date spikes (e.g. returning after a week off); when cards are hidden by the limit, the congratulations screen suggests raising it if you have time.

string.name: deck_learnSteps_help
string.value:
Delays during new-card learning, entered as positive numbers of minutes separated by spaces. For example, 1 10 means 1 minute then 10 minutes; enter 0.5 for 30 seconds or 120 for 2 hours. This field does not accept s, m, h or d suffixes.

Again returns to the first step; Good advances; Hard usually averages the first two delays on the first step and repeats the current step later. Easy can skip remaining steps.
SM-2 uses the graduating interval after learning. FSRS calculates subsequent intervals from its memory model and can schedule short-term learning when steps are empty. For manual FSRS steps, prefer short delays you can complete within one study day.

string.name: deck_relearnSteps_help
string.value:
Relearning delays after rating a review card Again. Enter positive numbers of minutes separated by spaces, without unit suffixes; for example, 10 means 10 minutes.

With SM-2, empty steps skip fixed relearning steps; the next interval depends on the lapse multiplier, minimum lapse interval and other limits, rather than always being 1 day. FSRS computes intervals from memory state and may still schedule short-term relearning when steps are empty.

string.name: deck_newPerDayMinimum_help
string.value: A reserved field marked “currently unused” in the official Anki protocol. Setting it has no effect on scheduling today; it is shown only for compatibility with older deck presets. No need to change it.

string.name: deck_graduatingIntervalGood_help
string.value:
How many days to wait after a new card passes its final learning step with Good before it appears as a review card.
Example: 1 means it graduates today and first appears as a review tomorrow; 3 means it appears 3 days later.
This is a legacy SM-2 option; with FSRS enabled it no longer applies (FSRS computes the first review timing itself).

string.name: deck_graduatingIntervalEasy_help
string.value:
SM-2 only: Easy skips remaining learning steps, graduates the card and uses this first review interval in days. For example, 4 normally makes the card due about 4 days later.
It is recommended to keep this at least as long as the Good graduating interval; the form does not enforce a relationship between the two fields. This option does not apply with FSRS.

string.name: deck_newCardInsertOrder_help
string.value:
Controls the initial position (due number) new cards get; lower numbers are learned first. Existing new cards are repositioned when you change this.
“Due order”: first added, first learned. “Random”: new cards get random positions.
Official advice: with the v3 scheduler, keep “Due order” and control draw order via “New card gather order” instead.

string.name: deck_newCardGatherPriority_help
string.value:
The order used to gather new cards before reaching daily limits:

• Deck: subdecks in name order, then ascending position within each.
• Deck, then random notes: the same deck-name order, with random notes within each deck.
• Lowest / highest position: ascending / descending new-card position.
• Random notes: choose notes randomly and gather their cards, subject to limits and burying rules.
• Random cards: choose cards randomly.

Deck order here does not follow manual dragging on Home. Prefix names with 001, 002, etc. to influence gathering order. New-card display order can reorder the gathered cards afterward.

string.name: deck_newCardSortOrder_help
deck_newMix_help
string.value:
When new cards appear relative to reviews: mixed with reviews / after reviews / before reviews.
Example: “After reviews” clears today's due reviews before any new cards; “Before reviews” teaches new cards first.

string.name: deck_interdayLearningMix_help
string.value:
Places interday learning cards mixed with, before or after review cards.
Interday learning cards enter the day-based queue when a step crosses the study-day boundary; the delay need not be a full 24 hours. This does not order intraday learning cards waiting for a short delay.

string.name: deck_minimumLapseInterval_help
string.value:
SM-2 only: the minimum review interval after a lapse, normally 1 day, also constrained by the maximum review interval. It does not set fixed relearning-step delays or guarantee a 1-day interval after every lapse.
FSRS does not use this minimum.

string.name: deck_leechThreshold_help
string.value:
After a review card is answered Again this many times in total, it is marked as a leech.
Example: 8 means the card becomes a leech on its 8th lapse.
Leeches consume a lot of time. Official advice: rewrite the card, delete it, or devise a mnemonic for it.

string.name: deck_leechAction_help
string.value:
When the leech threshold is reached:

• Tag only: add leech to the note and keep scheduling the card.
• Suspend card: add the tag and suspend the current card until manually restored.

Search for tag:leech in Browse to find and improve these notes.

string.name: deck_reviewOrder_help
string.value:
Controls the display order of gathered review cards, using due date, deck, interval, ease, retrievability or random order.

• Due date ascending: earlier due cards first.
• Interval ascending / descending: shorter / longer intervals first.
• Ease ascending / descending: lower / higher ease first; lower ease generally means harder cards under SM-2.
• Retrievability ascending: cards predicted to be harder to recall first.
• Retrievability descending: cards predicted to be easier to recall first.
• Random: shuffle the order.

Sorting does not raise daily review limits or recalculate due dates.

string.name: deck_buryNew_help
string.value:
When on: other “new” cards from the same note (e.g. reverse cards, adjacent clozes) won't appear today and roll over to tomorrow.
Example: a note generates both “Front→Back” and “Back→Front” new cards; after you learn the front one today, the back one arrives tomorrow.

string.name: deck_buryReviews_help
string.value:
When on: other “review” cards from the same note won't appear today and roll over to tomorrow.
Example: with two review cards from one note, only one appears today, so neither answer spoils the other.

string.name: deck_buryInterdayLearning_help
string.value:
Automatically buries eligible interday-learning siblings to avoid showing related answers on the same day.
A step becomes interday learning when it crosses the study-day boundary and enters the day-based queue. It does not mean an interval over 1 day; even less than 24 hours can cross the boundary. Intraday learning cards are unaffected.

string.name: deck_disableAutoplay_help
string.value:
When on, card audio no longer plays automatically; tap the play button manually.
Example: enable it in libraries or at night so flipping a card never makes sudden noise.

string.name: deck_skipQuestionWhenReplayingAnswer_help
string.value:
When replaying answer audio, the question part of the audio is skipped.
Example: a card has “question recording + answer recording”; replaying the answer plays only the answer part.

string.name: deck_waitForAudio_help
string.value:
For regular flashcard Auto Advance, wait for audio to finish before actions such as showing the answer, rating or reminding. The configured delay must also have elapsed.
Choice cards use their own grading-feedback and continuation flow, independent of this option.

string.name: deck_capAnswerTimeToSecs_help
string.value:
The cap (seconds) applied when recording how long an answer took; longer times are recorded as the cap.
Example: the default 60 means a card pondered for 3 minutes is recorded as 60 seconds, keeping study statistics sane when you step away mid-card.

string.name: deck_showTimer_help
string.value:
Shows the time spent on the current card on the study page.
Example: enable it to pace yourself, e.g. answering within 15 seconds per card.

string.name: deck_stopTimerOnAnswer_help
string.value: Freeze the on-screen timer when the answer is shown. Study statistics still include time until you grade the answer.

string.name: deck_secondsToShowQuestion_help
string.value:
For regular flashcards, wait this many seconds on the question side before the question action. 0 disables it. Start or pause Auto Advance in Study > More.
Choice cards do not use this timer.

string.name: deck_secondsToShowAnswer_help
string.value:
For regular flashcards, wait this many seconds on the answer side before the answer action. 0 disables it. Start Auto Advance in Study > More first.
Choice cards use their own feedback delay instead of this setting.

string.name: deck_questionAction_help
string.value: For regular flashcards, show the answer or a reminder when the question timer expires. A reminder does not flip the card. Auto Advance must be started first. Choice cards do not use this action.

string.name: deck_answerAction_help
string.value:
For regular flashcards, skip today, rate Again / Good / Hard, or show a reminder when the answer timer expires. Auto Advance must be started first.
Choice cards rate automatically from the grading result instead of using this action.

string.name: deck_desiredRetention_help
string.value:
FSRS schedules cards to become due near this predicted recall probability. The default is 0.9 (90%).
Higher values usually shorten intervals and increase reviews; lower values reduce reviews with more forgetting. Workload rises sharply near 100%, so adjust conservatively and generally stay below 0.97. This is a scheduling target, not a guarantee of an identical measured success rate.

string.name: deck_fsrsParams4_help
string.value:
FSRS 4 parameters are used to calculate memory state and review intervals. Avoid entering arbitrary values or copying another person’s parameters.

Scheduling uses the first non-empty set in this order: v6, v5, then v4. Defaults apply only if all three sets are empty; clearing v6 alone may activate older parameters.
This app can save these parameters but has no Optimize or Evaluate button. To fit parameters to your review history, use an Anki client that supports optimization and sync afterward.

string.name: deck_easyDaysPercentages_help
string.value:
Set review-load preferences for the week with seven values from 0 to 1, Monday through Sunday.

1 means Normal and 0 means Minimum. All other values mean Reduced; use 0.5 for clarity. A value of 0.4 does not mean exactly 40% of reviews.
Scheduling adjusts only within allowed date ranges, so it cannot guarantee zero reviews or an exact percentage on a given day.

string.name: deck_fsrsParams5_help
string.value:
FSRS 5 parameters are used to calculate memory state and review intervals. Avoid entering arbitrary values or copying another person’s parameters.

Scheduling uses the first non-empty set in this order: v6, v5, then v4. Defaults apply only if all three sets are empty; clearing v6 alone may activate older parameters.
This app can save these parameters but has no Optimize or Evaluate button. To fit parameters to your review history, use an Anki client that supports optimization and sync afterward.

string.name: deck_fsrsParams6_help
string.value:
FSRS 6 parameters are used to calculate memory state and review intervals. Avoid entering arbitrary values or copying another person’s parameters.

Scheduling uses the first non-empty set in this order: v6, v5, then v4. Defaults apply only if all three sets are empty; clearing v6 alone may activate older parameters.
This app can save these parameters but has no Optimize or Evaluate button. To fit parameters to your review history, use an Anki client that supports optimization and sync afterward.

string.name: deck_historicalRetention_help
string.value:
When older review history is incomplete, FSRS uses this assumed historical retention to estimate memory state. The default is 0.9.
It is an input assumption, not a measured success rate or the current desired retention. Usually keep the default unless you have a specific reason to change it.

string.name: deck_paramSearch_help
string.value:
An Anki search query selecting cards for FSRS parameter optimization. When empty, optimization uses non-suspended cards in the current preset; otherwise it uses the specified query.

This app saves the setting but has no Optimize button. Editing it does not start training or change the Browse query.

string.name: deck_initialEase_help
string.value:
The starting ease factor assigned when a card graduates under SM-2, normally 2.5 (250%).
The first interval is set by the graduating-interval option and is not multiplied by 2.5. Ease affects later review intervals and changes with ratings. FSRS does not use this option.

string.name: deck_easyMultiplier_help
string.value:
In the legacy algorithm, the extra interval multiplier applied when answering Easy (default 1.3).
Example: with a 10-day interval and ease 2.5, Easy gives ≈ 10 × 2.5 × 1.3 = 32.5 days. Only applies when FSRS is disabled.

string.name: deck_hardMultiplier_help
string.value:
In the legacy algorithm, the interval multiplier applied when answering Hard (default 1.2).
Example: with a 10-day interval, Hard gives ≈ 10 × 1.2 = 12 days. Only applies when FSRS is disabled.

string.name: deck_lapseMultiplier_help
string.value:
SM-2 only: after Again on a review card, multiply the old interval by this factor, then apply the minimum lapse interval and other constraints.
The default 0 reduces the interval to the applicable minimum; it does not reset the card to new or erase its history. FSRS does not use this option.

string.name: deck_intervalMultiplier_help
string.value:
A multiplier for passing review intervals under SM-2, normally 1. For example, 1.1 tends to lengthen intervals and 0.9 shortens them; rounding, random variation and interval limits still apply. Lapse intervals use separate settings, and FSRS does not use this multiplier.
This is a deck-preset option whose save scope follows the shared-deck setting, not a collection-wide switch.

string.name: deck_maximumReviewInterval_help
string.value:
The upper limit in days when calculating review intervals, normally 36500 days.
For example, 365 caps newly calculated review intervals at 365 days. Whether a card is actually shown on its due date also depends on studying, daily limits and states such as suspension.

string.name: deck_ignoreRevlogsBeforeDate_help
string.value:
Enter YYYY-MM-DD to ignore earlier reviews when FSRS trains parameters or computes memory state from history. Leave empty for no date cutoff. This does not delete records or hide them from ordinary review statistics.

The cutoff also affects initialization of cards without memory state and memory recalculation triggered by parameter changes. Changing only this date does not necessarily recalculate every card immediately. This app has no Optimize or Evaluate button.

string.name: add_note_deck_help
string.value:
Which deck this card is saved into. The deck you were viewing before opening this page is selected by default.
Example: to put a vocabulary card into the “English::CET-4” subdeck, open the dropdown and pick that deck; deck hierarchy is shown with “::”.
Changing the deck only affects where this card is saved, not its content.

string.name: add_note_notetype_help
string.value:
The note type decides which fields this note has and which card templates are generated; the field list below updates when you change it.
Example: “Basic” has just Front/Back fields and makes 1 card; “Basic (and reversed card)” also makes a reverse card; “Cloze” hides text marked {{c1::...}}.
Tip: after switching types, fill fields per their names; saving fails if a required field is empty.

string.name: add_note_notetype_basic_help
string.value:
Purpose: the most basic Q&A note type — one question, one answer. Good for simple memorization like vocabulary, concepts, definitions.
Difference from type-in-the-answer: Basic review is mental recall only; you do not type the answer.
Generates 1 card (Front → Back). During review you see Front, recall Back mentally, then flip to verify.
Field effects: Front holds the question (e.g. “apple”); Back holds the answer (e.g. “apple’s translation”).

string.name: add_note_notetype_basic_reversed_help
string.value:
Purpose: bidirectional Q&A note type. Good for content that must be drilled both ways, e.g. bilingual word pairs.
Difference from plain Basic: an extra reverse card is generated so both directions are tested.
Generates 2 cards (Front → Back + Back → Front). One card asks Front and answers Back; the other is reversed.
Field effects: Front holds the question (e.g. “apple”); Back holds the answer (e.g. “apple’s translation”). Both fields are shared by the two cards.

string.name: add_note_notetype_basic_optional_reversed_help
string.value:
Purpose: optional bidirectional Q&A — decide per note whether to generate the reverse card. Good for mixed decks where only some items need both directions.
Difference from Basic (and reversed card): the reverse card is not always on; the third field Add Reverse controls whether a reverse card is generated.
By default generates 1 forward card (Front → Back); when Add Reverse = “1” or “y”, an extra reverse card (Back → Front) is generated, 2 cards in total.
Field effects: Front holds the question (e.g. “apple”); Back holds the answer (e.g. “apple’s translation”); Add Reverse = “1” or “y” to generate the reverse card, leave empty for forward only.

string.name: add_note_notetype_cloze_help
string.value:
[Purpose] Fill-in-the-blank note type. Delete text in place to test recall. Good for memorizing source text, definitions, example sentences.

[c1–c5 button usage]
① Type the source text in the Text field;
② Select the part to delete;
③ Tap c1/c2/c3/c4/c5 — it wraps the selection as {{cN::selected text}}.
With no selection, tapping inserts an empty marker {{cN::}} and places the cursor right after the colon for typing.

[c index semantics]
· All markers sharing the same c index → deleted together on the same card;
· Different c indices → different cards (c1 is card 1, c2 is card 2, ...).
Example: The {{c1::capital}} of {{c1::France}} is {{c2::Paris}}
  · Card 1 (c1): The [...] of [...] is Paris
  · Card 2 (c2): The capital of France is [...]
This design supports progressive learning — c1 deletes big chunks (learn the whole first), c2/c3 delete details (drill finer points later).

[Difference from Q&A] No separate question is needed; deletions are the questions. One note generates as many cards as distinct c indices.

[Field effects]
· Text: source text with {{c1::answer}} marks, e.g. “The capital of France is {{c1::Paris}}”. During review c1 shows as [...]; recall Paris then flip to reveal.
· Extra: notes or examples, usually left empty.

string.name: add_note_notetype_basic_type_answer_help
string.value:
A one-card question-and-answer type for active typing, such as spelling or dictation.

Front contains the question and Back the correct answer. The input box appears on the question side. After showing the answer, the answer side compares your input with Back character by character.
The comparison helps you judge the answer; regular flashcards still require a rating based on your recall.

string.name: add_note_notetype_image_occlusion_help
string.value: Purpose: used to memorize by drawing masks on an image (e.g. anatomy labels, map place names). Suited for image-based memory. Difference from regular Q&A: image + masks replace text Q&A — instead of deleting text, you draw rectangles on the image to cover the regions to be tested. Each mask index generates one card. During review the mask covers the region; flip to reveal the underlying image. Field effects: pick an image, draw rectangular masks, optionally fill in header and extra. Image: after picking, the system writes it and fills for you, no manual entry. Occlusions: open the mask editor and draw one or more rectangles, each tied to a c index; the system auto-generates the {{c1::image-occlusion:rect:...}} string, no manual entry. Header: optional, a title shown at the top of the card (e.g. “Upper limb muscles”). Back Extra: optional, extra text shown after flipping.

string.value:
Tags for this note; separate multiple tags with spaces. Tags are independent of decks and are used for cross-deck search and filtering; “::” creates hierarchy.
Example: entering “english cet4::listening” adds both the “english” and “cet4::listening” tags, later searchable via tag:english or tag:cet4::listening.

string.name: deck_reviewLimit_help
string.value:
A daily review limit that applies only to this deck, overriding the preset; leave blank to follow the preset.
Example: with a preset of 200 reviews/day, entering 50 for the “Medicine” deck caps Medicine at 50 reviews a day, while decks using the preset are unaffected.

string.name: deck_newLimit_help
string.value:
A daily new-card limit that applies only to this deck, overriding the preset; leave blank to follow the preset.
Example: with a preset of 20 new cards/day, entering 5 for the “Speaking” deck introduces at most 5 new cards there each day.

string.name: deck_reviewToday_help
string.value:
A review limit for the current study day. Enter a value, turn on the corresponding switch and save; 0 gives no allowance for that category today.
Saving with an empty value or the switch off clears the override. It expires at the next study day, falling back to this deck’s limit, then the preset if no deck limit is set. Study days may not change at midnight.

string.name: deck_newToday_help
string.value:
A new-card limit for the current study day. Enter a value, turn on the corresponding switch and save; 0 gives no allowance for that category today.
Saving with an empty value or the switch off clears the override. It expires at the next study day, falling back to this deck’s limit, then the preset if no deck limit is set. Study days may not change at midnight.

string.name: deck_reviewTodayActive_help
string.value:
Turn on and save to apply today’s review limit. Turning it off keeps the number in the open form, but saving clears the override rather than storing a disabled temporary value.
After disabling or expiry, this deck’s limit applies first, with the preset used only when there is no deck override.

string.name: deck_newTodayActive_help
string.value:
Turn on and save to apply today’s new-card limit. Turning it off keeps the number in the open form, but saving clears the override rather than storing a disabled temporary value.
After disabling or expiry, this deck’s limit applies first, with the preset used only when there is no deck override.

string.name: deck_desiredRetentionOverride_help
string.value:
An FSRS desired retention that applies only to this deck, overriding the preset; leave blank to follow the preset.
Example: with a preset of 0.9, entering 0.95 for the “High-frequency exam points” deck schedules it more densely while other decks stay at 0.9.

string.name: deck_newCardsIgnoreReviewLimit_help
string.value:
By default, new cards stop appearing once the review limit is exhausted; when on, new cards appear regardless of the review limit.
Example: the 200-card review limit is fully consumed by reviews — with this on, new cards still appear today (making the day's total load heavier). This is a collection-wide setting affecting all decks.

string.name: deck_fsrsEnabled_help
string.value:
Enables FSRS for the entire collection, affecting every deck. FSRS uses memory state, ratings and desired retention to calculate intervals; turning it off uses SM-2.

This app has no parameter optimization button. Use a compatible Anki client to fit parameters and sync afterward if needed. All clients you use should support FSRS.

string.name: deck_applyAllParentLimits_help
string.value:
By default, studying from a child deck ignores the daily limits of decks above it; when on, limits apply level by level starting from the topmost deck.
Example: “Languages” (limit 50) contains “English” (limit 30); with this on, studying from English is also bounded by Languages' 50 — both levels constrain at once. Useful for capping an entire deck tree. This is a collection-wide setting.

string.name: deck_fsrsReschedule_help
string.value:
On save, also recalculate due dates for cards that need updating because of changes to parameters, desired retention, or related options. Leave off to avoid immediate rescheduling.
Changes apply only to this deck by default. Enabling shared changes also affects the related decks. Toggling the global FSRS switch affects all decks.
Large collections may take longer. Wait for saving to finish.

string.name: deck_fsrsHealthCheck_help
string.value:
Checks how well FSRS fits review history during parameter optimization. It is not a database repair or a scheduling repair performed on save.
This app only saves the preference and has no optimization entry; saving it here does not run a health check.

string.value: jidecards is open-source software that collects no user data, contains no in-app purchases or ads, and does not bundle any study or card content. You can find publicly shared decks on AnkiWeb, download them, and then import them into the app.

string.name: glossary_bury_help
string.value:
Skip this card for today. It becomes available again on the next study day.

Skip today is Anki's Bury action. It removes the card from today's study queue without deleting it. The study day follows the app's daily rollover time, which may differ from midnight.

Use it when you want to skip a card today. If you forgot the answer, choose Again so scheduling reflects your recall.

Unlike Suspend card, Skip today restores availability automatically.

To restore it sooner, choose Restore skipped cards on the study completion screen, or select it in Browse and use Restore Cards. The deck options for burying siblings apply the same action automatically to avoid related cards revealing each other's answers.

string.name: glossary_suspend_help
string.value:
Stop reviewing this card until you manually restore it.

This is Anki's Suspend action. It affects the current card, without pausing the whole study session or deleting the card.

Use it for cards you do not need to study for a while. To skip only today, use Skip today. If you forgot the answer, choose Again.

To restore the card, select it in Browse and use Restore Cards.

A card cannot be both buried and suspended. Suspending a skipped card prevents its automatic restoration.

string.name: glossary_delete_help
string.value:
Deletes the current card while keeping other cards of the same note. If no cards remain, the note is also deleted. Confirmation is required.

Use More > Undo at the top right of Study for the currently available undo action. Undo history does not persist across app sessions and may be cleared by syncing or closing the collection.

string.name: glossary_undo_help
string.value:
Undo the previous action, such as a rating, Skip today, Suspend card, or deletion. This corresponds to Anki's Undo.

On the study screen, open More > Undo. It is available when there is an action to undo.

Undo history does not persist across app sessions.

string.name: glossary_ratings_help
string.value:
For regular flashcards, recall the answer, show it, then rate your recall.

Again: You forgot or answered incorrectly.
Hard: You answered correctly with difficulty.
Good: You recalled the answer normally.
Easy: You answered correctly without effort.

The time below each button estimates when this card will be reviewed again if you choose that rating. Rate your recall, rather than the delay you prefer.

Choice cards use a separate flow: select and submit, then the app automatically rates a correct answer Good and an incorrect answer Hard. The regular four rating buttons are not shown. These automatic ratings also enter review statistics.

string.name: glossary_leech_help
string.value:
A review card is marked as a leech after it has been rated "Again" a certain number of times (default 8, configurable via "Leech Threshold").

Action options: Tag Only (adds a "leech" tag to the note, card still appears) / Suspend Card (hides the card until manually unsuspended).

Leeches consume a lot of time. Anki official advice: rewrite the card, delete it, or think of a mnemonic — don't just keep lapsing on it.

Configurable via deck options "Leech Threshold" and "Leech Action".

string.name: glossary_siblings_help
string.value:
Siblings are cards generated from the same note, such as forward/reverse cards or different cloze deletions in one passage.

Deck options can separately bury new, review and interday-learning siblings to avoid revealing answers on the same day. Interday learning means the delay crosses the study-day boundary and enters the day-based queue; it need not exceed 24 hours.
Siblings still in intraday learning are not automatically buried by these options.

string.name: glossary_graduating_interval_help
string.value:
The first interval applied when a new card finishes its last learning step and becomes a review card.

Graduating on "Good": uses "Graduating Interval (Good)" (default 1 day, i.e. appears tomorrow as a review card)
Graduating on "Easy": skips remaining steps, uses "Graduating Interval (Easy)" (default 4 days)

This is an SM-2 option; with FSRS enabled, the first review timing is computed by FSRS and this option no longer applies.

string.name: glossary_fsrs_retention_help
string.value:
FSRS desired retention is the predicted recall probability at which cards are scheduled to become due, normally 0.9 (90%).

Higher values generally increase reviews and lower values increase forgetting. Adjust conservatively and generally stay below 0.97. The target is not the measured retention shown in statistics.
Set the preset target in deck options, or enter an override for the current deck.

string.name: glossary_fuzz_help
string.value:
After a review card's next due date is computed from the rating, Anki applies a small random offset so cards introduced at the same time with the same rating don't always fall on the same day and cluster together.

Learning cards also receive up to 5 minutes of extra delay so they don't always appear in the same order (the next-due text on the rating buttons does not reflect this delay).

Official note: this feature cannot be turned off.

string.name: glossary_shortcuts_help
string.value:
Physical-keyboard shortcuts for regular flashcards:

• Space / Enter: show the answer on the question side; rate Good on the answer side.
• 1 / 2 / 3 / 4: rate Again / Hard / Good / Easy on the answer side.
• * or B: skip today.
• @ or S: suspend the card.
• Delete: delete the current card with confirmation.
• Ctrl+Z: undo the available action.
• Esc: go back.
• R: replay audio. On the answer side, the Skip question when replaying answer option applies; with it off, question audio is included.

Choice cards require selecting and submitting an answer for automatic grading; regular flip and 1–4 rating shortcuts do not answer them.

string.name: glossary_lapse_help
string.value:
Rating a review card Again causes a lapse and adds 1 to its lapse count. Reaching the leech threshold triggers the configured leech action.

With fixed relearning steps, the card follows those delays. SM-2 then uses the lapse multiplier, minimum lapse interval and other constraints. FSRS calculates from memory state instead of those two legacy options, and may schedule short-term relearning even with empty steps.

string.name: glossary_browser_info_help
string.value:
Tap the ⓘ on a card row in Browse to view its card type (template name), deck, due information, interval, review and lapse counts, available FSRS memory information, and review history.

Card type is not the card’s new, suspended or buried state. This panel is read-only; tap the row to edit its content.

string.name: sync_help_text
string.value:
Sync now checks the server and synchronizes card data in both directions. If a full replacement is required, you choose upload or download.

Leave the server address blank for AnkiWeb. A custom server must support Anki 26.05. Enter its base URL (for example, http://192.168.1.200:8080/ or https://example.com/anki/), then sign in with its own account. Separate collection and media URLs are not needed. Log out before changing servers; logging out keeps local cards.

Automatic sync is on by default. Once signed in, it runs on startup, foreground resume, or return to the home page. It waits for studying, editing, and importing to end, and combines repeated triggers. Success closes automatically; errors stay visible, and full-sync conflicts can be postponed.

Turn off Sync media to sync card data without audio and images.

string.name: browser_help_sidebar_body
string.value:
Open Filter to browse decks, tags and saved searches.

• Tap a deck or tag to replace the query in the search box.
• Long-press a deck to append an AND condition.
• Long-press a tag to open its action menu, then choose Append to search. The menu also offers tag actions such as rename and delete.
• Saved searches use queries stored in the collection, such as those synced from Anki desktop.
• Sections can be collapsed or expanded, and their state is saved.

string.name: browser_help_find_replace_body
string.value:
Batch-replace text in note fields. Editing a note affects every card generated from it.

Inputs
• Find: plain text or a regular expression; an empty value does nothing.
• Replace with: leave empty to delete matching text.
• Field name: leave empty for all fields, or specify a name such as Front or Back. This feature does not replace tags; Tags is treated only as a field name.
• Regex: use $1, $2, etc. in the replacement to reference capture groups.
• Match case: when on, Cat and cat are different.

Scope
• Selected notes only: use the selected notes, or the distinct notes belonging to selected cards.
• Current search results: use the complete results at the time you execute, including rows not yet loaded by scrolling. The search query and status filter both apply. Empty results do nothing; later searches do not change an accepted operation.

Example: search for deck:Swahili, choose Current search results, then replace color with colour.

Undo
Replacement is recorded in the current session’s undo history. Browse has no direct Undo button; check the available action in Study > More > Undo. Syncing or closing the collection may clear undo history. Confirm the scope before executing instead of relying on undo.

string.name: browser_help_batch_body
string.value:
Long-press a row to select cards or notes for batch actions.

Change deck / Flag
Moving cards preserves their scheduling state. Flags (none, red, orange, green or blue) do not affect scheduling. In Notes mode, these actions apply to every card generated by the selected notes.

Suspend / Restore
Suspended cards leave the study queue. Restore Cards restores both suspended and buried cards. In Notes mode, every card of the selected notes is affected.

Delete
Cards mode deletes selected cards and removes a note if no cards remain. Notes mode deletes all cards and the selected notes.
Deletion enters the current session’s undo history, but Browse has no direct Undo button. Check Study > More > Undo for the available action. Syncing or closing the collection may clear history; confirm before deleting.

Set Due Date: Cards mode only
Enter 60 or 60-90 for a date that many days from now; dates within a range are assigned randomly. New cards become review cards.
Review cards without an FSRS memory state normally retain their interval unless ! is appended. Cards with an FSRS memory state recalculate their interval using the last review time and new due date, so the old interval is not guaranteed. This does not count as answering a card, but changes future-due and interval statistics.

Reposition: Cards mode only
Only new-card positions change. Positions are assigned per note as start + index × step; selected cards of the same note share a position. Random shuffles the notes before assignment, rather than picking a random number inside each step.
Shift existing moves existing new cards at or after the insertion position back. Without it, positions may overlap. Gather and display order settings still control presentation.

Change Note Type
Map old fields and templates to the new type. Unmapped field contents are lost. Retained, mapped cards can keep their schedule; unmapped cards may be deleted and new templates may generate new cards.
A full sync is required afterward. Choose an available direction in the sync screen; downloading replaces local changes with server data.

string.name: browser_find_regex_help
string.value:
When enabled, Find matches a regular expression against field text. • Character classes: [a-z], \d, \w, \s • Repetition: *, +, ?, {n,m} • ^ and $ match the start and end of the entire field by default. Add (?m) for line-by-line matching. HTML
is not a newline character. • Capture groups: use () and reference them with $1, $2, etc. in the replacement; use $$ for a literal dollar sign. • Escape special characters such as ., * and ( with a preceding backslash. Examples: \d+ matches digits; (?m)^hello.* matches text lines starting with hello; replace (\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2}) with $3/$2/$1 to reformat dates.

string.name: stats_help_today
string.value:
Studied counts answers. Due includes overdue cards, excludes new cards and is not capped by daily study limits.

Today’s counts:
• Answered: ratings submitted today; one card may count more than once.
• Correct: submissions rated Hard, Good or Easy.
• Learn / Review / Relearn / Filtered: categories of answer records.
• Mature success: the proportion of non-Again ratings among records with a prior interval of at least 21 days.
• Time: the recorded answer time counted for today.

Choice cards use automatically submitted ratings. An incorrect choice rated Hard also counts as correct under this definition; this is not choice-answer accuracy. Daily counts describe today’s records, not overall mastery.

string.name: stats_help_forecast
string.value:
Summarizes future due counts from current schedules; it does not simulate new schedules after future answers.

• The X-axis shows future dates. Longer ranges may combine several days into one bar; height is the total for that day or date interval.
• Dark-to-light green marks nearer-to-later dates.
• Total counts cards in the displayed range; Average uses its date span.
• Due tomorrow counts cards due tomorrow.
• Daily load estimates the sum of 1/interval in days, treating intervals under 1 day as 1. It estimates long-term workload rather than tomorrow’s exact count.
• When backlog exists, check Backlog to show overdue cards on the left. Without it, those bars are hidden.

New and suspended cards are excluded, and daily study limits do not cap this forecast.

string.name: stats_help_card_counts
string.value:
Shows card counts within the selected statistics scope.

• New: unstudied cards.
• Learning / Relearning: cards in initial learning or relearning after a lapse.
• Young / Mature: review intervals under 21 days / at least 21 days.
• Suspended: cards paused manually or by actions such as leech handling.
• Buried: cards skipped for today, available again next study day.

With Separate suspended/buried cards enabled, the last two groups are counted separately. Otherwise, those cards remain in the first five groups by card type. Bar lengths show proportions; the table lists counts and percentages.

string.name: stats_help_hours
string.value:
Counts answers by hour of day within the selected time range.

• The X-axis runs from hour 0 to 23.
• Bar height is the number of eligible answers during that hour; repeated answers to one card count separately.
• Higher counts use darker blue.

Filtered early-review, manual scheduling and rescheduling records are excluded. The graph shows when you tend to study, not a count of distinct cards.

string.name: stats_help_ease
string.value:
Shows card ease or difficulty, with bar height representing the number of cards in each bin.

• SM-2: the X-axis is ease, from 130% to around the maximum in the current data, not a fixed 390%. Higher ease generally means easier cards; colors run red, yellow, then green.
• FSRS: the X-axis is difficulty expressed from 0% to 100%. Higher means harder; colors run green, yellow, then red.

The average uses the metric of the current algorithm. Values from the two algorithms are not directly comparable.

string.name: stats_help_interval
string.value:
Intervals
Shows the distribution of current review intervals.

· X-axis: review interval (days), short on the left to long on the right
· Y-axis (bar height): number of cards in that interval range
· Bar colour: light → dark blue marks short → long intervals (colour only marks the interval range; bar height is the card count)

Interval = the delay between two reviews. Independent of FSRS: this graph always shows actual card intervals (Anki official Review Intervals).

The time range setting affects this graph differently: it limits displayed interval range, not which cards are included.

string.name: stats_help_stability
string.value:
Stability
Only shown when FSRS is enabled.

· X-axis: stability (days), low on the left to high on the right
· Y-axis (bar height): number of cards in that stability range
· Bar colour: light → dark blue marks low → high stability (colour only marks the stability range; bar height is the card count)

Stability = the amount of time required for the probability of recall to decrease from 100% to 90%. Higher stability = less likely to be forgotten (Anki official Card Stability). Note: intervals reflect actual scheduling, while stability reflects memory strength.

string.name: stats_help_retention
string.value:
Pass rates for eligible answers within each time window.

• Hard, Good and Easy count as passes; Again counts as a failure.
• The interval before the answer determines young (under 21 days) versus mature (at least 21 days).
• Rated review records that affect scheduling are included. Other learning or relearning records may also count when their previous interval is at least 1 day. Manual rescheduling and preview reviews that do not affect scheduling are excluded.
• Every eligible record is counted; there is no first-review-per-card-per-day deduplication.

Measured retention may differ from the FSRS target; prefer longer time windows. Choice cards are counted by their submitted automatic rating, so this is not a choice-answer accuracy measure.

string.name: stats_help_retrievability
string.value:
Shown when FSRS is enabled. It estimates the probability of recalling cards today.

• Average retrievability: the mean for cards in the selected scope that have an FSRS memory state.
• Estimated known cards: the sum of those recall probabilities.
• Estimated known notes: average the probabilities across each note’s cards, then sum the note averages. Sibling cards do not count as separate notes; cards without memory state contribute zero to their note.
• The X-axis is retrievability, bar height is the card count in each bin, and red, yellow and green indicate increasing recall probability.

These are model estimates, not individual checks that you remember every card.

string.name: stats_help_calendar
string.value:
Calendar
A yearly heatmap of daily review counts.

· Each cell is one day: columns are weeks, rows are weekdays; darker color = more reviews that day
· Use ◄ ► to browse previous years (back to 2000 with All-time range)
· Tap a weekday label on the left to change the first day of week (Sunday/Monday/Friday/Saturday)

Matches the Anki official Calendar graph.

string.name: stats_help_reviews
string.value:
Reviews
Daily review counts as a stacked bar chart (Anki official Reviews).

· X-axis: dates, oldest on the left to newest on the right
· Y-axis (bar height): review count per day (or time spent answering when 'Time' is checked)
· Each bar is one day (or a few days merged)
· Stack bottom-up: mature (dark green), young (light green), relearn (red), learn (orange), filtered (purple)
· Check 'Time' to switch to the time taken to answer the questions each day
· Bottom stats: days studied, total, average per day, average on studied days; time mode adds average answer time (seconds/card + cards/minute)

Matches the Anki official Reviews graph.

string.name: stats_help_buttons
string.value:
Shows submitted rating counts for a selectable history range, defaulting to one year.

• Learning includes learning, relearning and filtered records. Young and Mature use review intervals before the answer of under 21 days and at least 21 days.
• Each group is ordered Again, Hard, Good, Easy; bar height is the count.
• Colors are red, yellow, light green and dark green.
• The success rate below counts every rating other than Again as correct.

Choice cards submit ratings automatically (Good for correct, Hard for incorrect), so this rate is not choice-answer accuracy and counts are not necessarily manual button presses.

string.name: stats_help_added
string.value:
Counts cards by creation date. Multiple cards generated by one note are counted separately.

• Dates run oldest to newest; longer ranges may combine several days in one bar.
• Height is the number of cards added on that day or within that date interval.
• Colors progress from light blue for older dates to dark blue for more recent dates.
• The summary shows the total and average added per day in the selected range.

string.name: home_intro_flashcards_title
string.value: What can flashcards help you learn?

string.name: home_intro_flashcards_body
string.value:
Flashcards put a question on the front and an answer on the back. Recall first, then reveal the answer. JideCards schedules spaced reviews based on your recall.

Practice vocabulary, languages, medicine, law, coursework, exams, history, or skills for work. Keep each card focused on one point.

string.name: home_intro_apkg_title
string.value: Import an APKG and start learning

string.name: home_intro_apkg_body
string.value:
An APKG (.apkg) is an Anki deck package that can include images and audio. Choose New deck → Import deck on the home screen, select the file, then open the deck to study.

Recall → Show answer → Rate your recall: Again, Hard, Good, or Easy. The times below the buttons are estimated review intervals. Complete your due reviews each day.

string.name: home_intro_agent_title
string.value: Create and edit cards with an Agent

string.name: home_intro_agent_body
string.value:
Try an Agent such as WorkBuddy or TRAE that can work with files and run code. Provide your notes or study materials, specify the scope, card count, and format, and ask for an importable .apkg file.

Create: “Make 20 question-and-answer cards from this material. Ask one point per card, keep answers short, and generate an APKG with the required media.”

Edit: export an APKG from More in the deck details, then ask: “Add explanations, shorten answers, and correct errors. Preserve note identifiers and media, and output an updated APKG.” Keep the original as a backup and check the result before importing. Changing identifiers or note types may create duplicates.
